correctness.rationale: The H² normalized-kernel identity yields f(w)=(1-|w|²)/(1-a w^m conjugate(w)); at |w|²=t, its circular fiber has center (1-t)/(1-q² t^(m+1)) and radius (1-t) q t^((m+1)/2)/(1-q²t^(m+1)). For q<1 logarithmic radius u=-log t gives R=(1-e^-u)/(2sinh(eta+alpha u)), and differentiation reduces its unique positive maximum to the strictly increasing function F(u)=atanh[alpha(e^u-1)]-alpha u=eta. At q=1, R decreases from 1/(m+1), unachieved in the disk. Fiber phase equation yields exactly m-1 attaining kernels per imaginary sign for q<1. For small q a uniform maximizing-limit calculation yields the q coefficient; near q=1 expansion F(u)=alpha u²/2+O(u³) gives square-root width deficit 1/(sqrt2 alpha^(3/2)). Finally expansion f~u/(alpha u-i psi) proves the iff angular/radial ratio at all extremizing sequences. Strict q- and m-monotonicity follows from radius comparison, whereas ordinary Berezin number is 1.
residual_risks: The limiting extremizer characterization uses principal phase control psi=O(u); no claim of full 2D range shape.
Finite optimizer samples do not establish global uniqueness; that is analytically given by strict derivative F'>0.
